server.privacy_lead: This page describes what data the VocabBot server stores and why.
privacy: The server stores your username, a hash of your password (scrypt), your learning plan, the log of answers, your own words, notes on words, words set aside and reports of mistakes in the course. It also stores the time zone your browser reported when you created the account. No name is required.

An e-mail address is optional and is used only for password recovery. The server stores only its hash (scrypt), so it cannot read the address or send it anything other than a link you request by entering that address.

A learning folder linked to the account with vocabbot login sends the server the same data as a session in a chat app: log entries with your typed answers, notes, your own words and changes to the plan. The server also records which apps and computers are connected to the account and when they last used it. You can disconnect any of them on the account page.

The session page in your browser stores one cookie for the signed-in session. If you choose a language with the switch, the server's pages also store a cookie with that choice. The server uses no advertising or analytics cookies.
A connected chat app, such as Claude or ChatGPT, processes the conversation under its own terms. The server receives from it only calls to VocabBot's tools, together with your answers.
Your data is used only for your learning. The server does not share or sell it. On the account page you can download all your data as an archive and delete the account together with the data.

server.hero_lead: VocabBot runs a daily vocabulary routine in one, two or three languages at once. Spaced repetition helps you retain every word, and you can study in Claude, ChatGPT, the terminal or your phone's browser. The A1 to B2 courses are designed for Polish speakers.
server.mock_caption: A sample session in a chat app, in Polish. The assistant leads the conversation, and VocabBot's engine grades the answers.
server.features_lead: The same engine grades your answers and schedules your reviews in every app. Every answer goes into one learning plan, whichever device you use.

features.title: Spaced repetition
features.text: The FSRS-6 algorithm schedules each review so that a word comes back before you forget it.

features.title: Up to three languages at once
features.text: English, German, Spanish, French and Italian, from A1 to B2. Words from your chosen languages are interleaved in a single session.

features.title: One account on every device
features.text: Your account connects the chat app, the terminal and your phone. A session started on one device can be finished on another.

features.title: The engine grades every answer
features.text: Grades, review dates and statistics come from VocabBot's engine. The assistant leads the conversation but cannot change a grade.

server.connect_title: Connect VocabBot to the assistant you already use
server.connect_lead: Add the server address in any app that supports MCP servers and sign in with the same account on every device.

connect_items.name: Claude
connect_items.steps: Open “Customize”, go to “Connectors”, choose “Add”, then “Add custom connector” and paste the server address.

connect_items.name: ChatGPT
connect_items.steps: Open `chatgpt.com/plugins`, click “+” and choose “Add custom MCP server”. Enter the server address and select OAuth authentication.

connect_items.name: Browser
connect_items.steps: The learning session is available at `/app/`. You can also add the page to your phone's home screen.

connect_items.name: Claude Code and Codex
connect_items.steps: Add the server with one command, then sign in through your browser: with `/mcp` in Claude Code or with `codex mcp login vocabbot` in Codex.

server.cta_lead: Accounts are created with an invitation code from the server administrator. You can set up your first learning plan in a few minutes, with or without a placement test.

server.faq_lead: Answers about the method, the courses, accounts and AI assistants.

faq.a: VocabBot is a vocabulary trainer based on spaced repetition. It runs a daily session in a chat app such as Claude or ChatGPT, in a terminal or in a browser. Its engine grades every answer and schedules the next review.
The courses cover English, German, Spanish, French and Italian from A1 to B2. A learning plan can include one, two or three languages at once. The courses are designed for Polish speakers.

Each word returns after a progressively longer interval. The FSRS-6 algorithm schedules a review so that the probability of a correct answer is 90% by default. A word answered incorrectly returns on the same day.

faq.q: Which apps does VocabBot work with?
faq.a: VocabBot works as a remote MCP server in Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code and Codex. You can also study in a browser at /app/ and in a terminal with the vocabbot program.

faq.q: Do I need a chat app to study?
faq.a: No. The session page works in desktop and mobile browsers, and the vocabbot program runs the same session in a terminal. Every way of studying uses one account and one learning plan.

faq.q: Can the AI assistant change a grade?
faq.a: No. VocabBot's engine grades answers according to the rules of each language. The assistant leads the conversation and explains meanings, but grades, review dates and statistics come only from the engine.

faq.q: How do I create an account?
faq.a: Accounts are created with an invitation code from the server administrator. After signing in, you can set up a learning plan with or without a placement test.

faq.q: Where do the courses come from?
faq.a: The courses are built from open data. Levels come from the CEFR-J wordlist, translations, forms and pronunciation from Wiktionary, word order from wordfreq, and example sentences from Tatoeba. The courses are available under the CC BY-SA 4.0 licence.
Yes. The code is available on GitHub under the Apache-2.0 licence. You can run the server yourself, and the vocabbot program also works offline.

faq.q: What data does the server store?
faq.a: The server stores your username, a password hash, your learning plan, the answer log, your own words and notes. On the account page you can download all your data and delete the account. The Privacy page has the details.
